title: Standings/records double-count overlapping Brasileirao seasons
evidence: soccer.cpp:45,49 both Brasileirao_Matches.csv (2012-2022) and novo_campeonato_brasileiro.csv (2003-2019) load with competition="Brasileirao"; standings() (soccer.cpp:65) and team_record() (soccer.cpp:64) filter by includes(m.competition,comp) so 2012-2019 matches are counted twice, roughly doubling points/records.
suggestion: Deduplicate matches on (date,home,away,season) at load time, or restrict one source to a non-overlapping season range.

title: No dataset-wide aggregate statistics (avg goals/match, biggest wins)
evidence: soccer.cpp exposes per-team team_record and per-competition standings, but no tool computes global stats like average goals per match or biggest victories cited in TASK.md:248-271; main.cpp:13 tool list has no such tool.
suggestion: Add an aggregate_stats tool computing avg goals/match and largest margins across the dataset.

title: ask_brazilian_soccer misroutes player-name queries through team list
evidence: soccer.cpp:68 answer() only searches players by a recognized team keyword (or the raw question) — 'Who is Gabriel Barbosa?' passes the full question as the name filter and won't match, since no team keyword is present.
suggestion: Extract the player name from the question (strip 'who is'/'jogador') and pass it as the name filter.

title: Matches with unparseable/empty dates render as 'NA' and sort to top
evidence: soccer.cpp:22 iso_date returns short strings unchanged; BR-Football-Dataset rows lacking a 10-char date yield empty m.date, printed as leading entries after descending date sort (see _agent_stdout.log item_11: 'NA: Flamengo 0-0 Athletico').
suggestion: Normalize the BR-Football-Dataset date column and drop or de-prioritize rows with no parseable date.

title: Hand-rolled regex JSON parsing is brittle for nested/escaped args
evidence: main.cpp:9-11 value()/integer()/arguments_object() use std::regex on raw request text rather than a JSON parser; nested objects or unusual escaping in arguments could be mis-extracted.
suggestion: Use a minimal JSON parser for the arguments object; acceptable for the flat schemas here but a latent risk.
